about: The capabilities (one module each) as src/admin/objects.ts moduleCatalog() reads them from src/modules/README.md, each README and tests/boundaries.json. The dependency rules below are the boundary test (tests/boundaries.test.ts).
rules: A capability never imports another capability's code: only src/shared/ and src/config/.
It reads another capability's output files through shared io and shared types.
A capability may import another's index.ts only for names listed in its readApi (read-only, side-effect free); the read-API graph is acyclic.
The orchestrator (production.ts, board.ts) imports only a module's index.ts and never writes a module's artifact: a write is the owning module's CLI as a child process.
The website imports a module only through its index.ts and readApi, plus src/orchestration/index.ts.
Browser-safe video files (remotion/, bespoke/, types, kinds, words, chart, cues, excerpt) import only other browser-safe entries, never node:*.
Every allowed exception is an exact edge in tests/boundaries.json with an until; the list is empty today and only shrinks.

dependencyKinds.cli-child: orchestration runs a module CLI as a child process (the only write path)
dependencyKinds.readApi: an import of named read-only exports
dependencyKinds.files: a read of another module's output files through shared io

modules.name: shared
modules.responsibility: src/shared/ (contracts, io, sentence validation, evidence gate, public record, look, build report, inspect), src/config/
modules.paths: src/shared/ (contracts, io, sentence validation, evidence gate, public record, look, build report, inspect), src/config/

d: channel and the topics it publishes
objects.writer: a person (topics claim adds the topic line)
objects.valid: only channels a person created; a topic is claimed by one commission; the fixture topic is fixtureTopics

d: automation.json: a closed key set, every
feature off by default; agent rules are code
objects.writer: a person
objects.valid: validated at build; agent permissions are never configuration (roles.ts); secrets stay in .env

modules.name: orchestration
modules.responsibility: Owns derived state: every topic's, story's and script's stage, computed from the committed artifacts alone (production.ts). Owns routing: for each story the stage, the next step (a command or a brief), the halt kind (HALT_KINDS) and the board column (COLUMNS, columnOf); publishing answers a structured next step (OutputStep: verb, actor, args, retryable); the board renders it (renderStep) and the runner dispatches on it. npm run board -- next <topic> <story-id> [--json] (board.ts) prints that answer; /produce (.claude/skills/produce/SKILL.md) is the executor of its steps. It reads each module through its index.ts (an inspect() where the module has one) and module files through src/shared/ io. The website reads it only through index.ts. It never writes a module's artifact, never judges content, and schedules nothing in Milestone 1. Milestone 2 adds the executor here (scheduling, execution of the board's steps as child processes and claude -p agents, retries, budgets, notifications, the approval mail adapter); those are coordination, and the two rules above still hold for them: a write is the owning module's CLI, and judgment is a brief handed to an agent. The runner (run/, npm run run -- story | status) is phase 0 of that: runner.ts is the loop over boardNext, steps.ts runs one step (a child with only its verb's secrets, or an agent followed by its validator), agent.ts and roles.ts spawn claude -p under per-role permission rules, guard.ts reverts writes outside a role's files and checks a graphics agent's components before a child loads them, journal.ts and lock.ts are its operational state under the story's gitignored run/, status.ts the read-only view the admin page may import through index.ts. It never publishes, posts, pushes or sends mail; it never imports a module file but its index.ts. Its only stored decision file is production.json (queued, parked); automation.json (Milestone 2) is policy, not state, and its operational files (run/, .automation/) are gitignored and decide no stage. The modules and their rules: src/modules/README.md.

d: their usage and cost, the batch, the mail
objects.writer: the discovery job (npm run run -- discover)
objects.valid: one record per weekly slot, written before any agent runs; a crash never doubles the batch or its mail

d: groups, fetched lists, study and review rounds
objects.writer: the topic runner (npm run run -- topic)
objects.valid: a resumed run never records a batch twice; two empty study rounds park the topic as thin

objects.writer: a person
objects.valid: queued and parked only; the one hand-written planning input

d: routed to the writer or to video-fix, once
objects.writer: the runner (npm run run -- story), from a request’s notes or --notes-file
objects.valid: once per request: a sentence or unplaced note to script -- send-back and the writer, a scene-only note to video-fix.md and video -- check

objects.writer: the release loop (draft-review.md agent)
objects.valid: no effect on any decision; the digest reads the agreement with the person and says whether agent may be enabled

d: validate, commit, push, probes, liveAt, posted
objects.writer: the launch job (npm run run -- launch) and the tick’s probe
objects.valid: resumable step by step; live only once the deploy probe answers; the X post after that, or not-configured

d: run/journal.jsonl: one line per step attempt;
halt.json: kind, why, unblock; lock.json: pid
objects.writer: the runners (story, topic, scan, article pass)
objects.valid: operational, gitignored, decides no stage; a halt names a command or a brief; a dead lock is taken over

d: call: models, tokens, cost, turns, exit
objects.writer: the step (steps.ts), open at spawn, complete at exit
objects.valid: usage and outcome only, never the prompt or the reply; failed and resumed kept; the unit every rollup and estimate sums

d: readiness.json: a person’s verification of an
integration, bound to evidence that exists
objects.writer: npm run run -- verified (a person; the only writer)
objects.valid: verification only; implemented is code, enabled is automation.json; a verification changes no flag

modules.name: article
modules.responsibility: Article owns editorial content through its lifecycle: drafting, review, validation, corrections and reaffirmations when evidence changes (article -- correct, reaffirm). Website renders article-release.json and never decides whether a finding needs a correction.

d: article-release.json is what the site shows
objects.writer: a writer agent (article.md); a different reviewer (article-review.md); lock, correct and reaffirm are the CLI’s
objects.valid: the script’s checks over its sentences plus coverage and overlap; only the release snapshot is rendered

d: text’s fingerprint; OK by reply releases it
objects.writer: npm run article -- request-correction (the pass), sent (the Message-ID), decide (a person)
objects.valid: bound to article.json’s fingerprint; a revision voids it; a correction is released only under a person’s name and appends a public-record revision

modules.name: brand
modules.responsibility: The brand kit builder: npm run brand (cli.ts, drawings in draw/draw.js, run in Remotion's headless Chrome).

modules.name: evidence
modules.responsibility: Evidence gathers and judges claims for a topic it is given; proposing or evaluating new topics is topic discovery (src/modules/topic-discovery/) and never evidence's job.
modules.paths: src/modules/evidence/ (topics.ts, corpus.ts, batches.ts, finding-label.ts, verdict-label.ts, cited.ts, datasets.ts, live-claims.ts)
modules.briefs: extract.md, sources.md, evidence.md, collect.md, studies.md, merge.md, revision-note.md

objects.writer: npm run record, record-sources, the watcher CLI
objects.valid: the store is the only truth of claims and verdicts; a hand edit is reverted by the tree guard

d: a video, post or study: store/videos/*.json
objects.writer: the watcher (fetch), evidence -- fetch-doc (a study)
objects.valid: a document saved only under sources/, https, a bare .txt name; a cite names a passage of it

d: shared by every source that makes it
objects.writer: npm run record from an extraction batch (h*.json)
objects.valid: one line, no numbers of one source; evidence belongs to the claim, so a new source never re-judges old claims

objects.writer: npm run record-sources from a study batch (sv_*.json)
objects.valid: one per claim and document; a study overrides an AI guess only when at least as confident; a cited pair is replaced only with --replace-cited by a person

objects.writer: npm run report
objects.valid: derived from the store; the build and the board read it; a stale one is regenerated, never edited

objects.writer: npm run report (exhibits, revisions), article -- correct (an article revision); the note is a person’s (report -- note)
objects.valid: exhibits never renumber; every revision needs a note or the build test fails

d: a cite per point; shown on /data/
objects.writer: a person or an agent, through the data brief
objects.valid: every point cites a passage; a tool’s defaults cite a dataset

d: maintenance.json: each scan, what it found
and recorded; due every everyDays days
objects.writer: npm run evidence -- scanned (from the scan job)
objects.valid: one entry per scan with found and recorded counts; lastScan decides when the next is due

modules.name: packaging
modules.responsibility: Packaging owns the review package of a rendered video: titles, descriptions, captions, chapters, the placement of the calls to action in the description, and the release metadata. Video owns the media and QA; the YouTube limits check (uploadProblem) is publishing's and packaging only calls it.

d: calls to action and X text one sha binds
objects.writer: npm run video -- package (a release build); packaging -- manifest rewrites it
objects.valid: releaseSha moves when an output is re-packaged, the article re-locked or a call to action changed, and voids the open request

modules.name: publishing
modules.responsibility: Publishing owns YouTube only: uploads, release approvals, scheduling, go-live, read-back and verification, recorded in the per-story ledger. Social (X and others) is a separate Milestone 2 module and never part of this one.

d: publish.json: per output an event log
objects.writer: npm run publish (every verb idempotent); metadata may be hand-edited
objects.valid: append-only events; a public upload needs a prior approved for that build; only a person approves or goes live

d: go-live; a Short is output short:<slug>
objects.writer: npm run publish -- upload, push, go-live, sync, verify (plain fetch, no googleapis)
objects.valid: upload sends private only; go-live needs approved; a Short goes live after its video; a live video is never replaced

d: decided by OK, OK at <when>, CHANGES: or the page
objects.writer: npm run publish -- request (automation), decide (a person, never automated:)
objects.valid: an rq- id signed with APPROVAL_SECRET; expired, decided or moved requests are refused; every step idempotent, decided last

modules.name: script
modules.responsibility: Script turns a reviewed story into the evidence package the writer may cite, validates the writer's script against it, and locks the approved fingerprints.

d: passages and roles a writer may use
objects.writer: npm run script -- package
objects.valid: built from stories.json and the store; its fingerprint binds the script; a moved package re-opens the review

objects.writer: a writer agent (script.md); a different reviewer (script-review.md); validate and lock are the CLI’s
objects.valid: every factual sentence carries an assertion; approvals by fingerprint; three revisions per pass; lock needs passed, storyboard ok, a real approver

modules.name: shorts
modules.responsibility: Shorts finds which findings of a produced video can stand on their own as a vertical Short, and builds the Short's evidence package as a filter of the parent's.

objects.writer: npm run shorts -- discover; the shorts.md agent reviews; the same CLIs produce it
objects.valid: shorts.json derived; at most 3 per video; its package is a filter of the parent’s; never touches the store

modules.name: social
modules.responsibility: X posts about a story's live outputs from the owning institution's account (Milestone 2, phase 3; spec §4.5's X row, §15). Optional per institution: an institution without an X handle or keys is "not configured", never a halt. Separate from publishing (YouTube): no coupling, no shared framework; the orchestration's launch probe runs post after the deploy is confirmed.
modules.paths: src/modules/social/ (social.ts the posts and their record, x.ts the X client)

d: social.json: an intent before the call, the
id after; once per text, never a fixture
objects.writer: npm run social -- post (the launch probe when enabled.social)
objects.valid: refused while enabled.social is off or the output is not live; not configured without a handle and keys; one post per textSha

modules.name: mail
modules.responsibility: The system's conversation with a person by email: one outbox (every mail sent, questions included), one received store (every mail that came back, correlated once to what it answers), an archive, and the verbs ask, send, fetch, questions, test. General communication (ask: the reply comes back as the person's own words, never read as authorisation) and formal authorisation (orchestration's request mails and reply grammar) ride the same records without sharing semantics. core/ is extraction-ready: it imports nothing outside itself (selfContained in tests/boundaries.json), is configured by an injected MailConfig and MailTransport, and knows kind: string and meta only.
modules.paths: src/modules/mail/ (core/: io, mutex, types, thread, transport, outbox, received, ask; cor.ts the Commonwealth adapter)

d: an outbox entry of kind question: sent to the
person, answered in their own words, acknowledged by the agent
objects.writer: npm run mail -- ask (a session or an authorised automation)
objects.valid: to the configured person only; status derived (unsent, failed, awaiting, unattended, answered); a timeout stops the waiter, never the question

d: received.json: every mail fetched, once, with the
sent mail it answers (correlated at record time)
objects.writer: npm run mail -- fetch (the only IMAP reader; ask runs it while waiting)
objects.valid: deduplicated by Message-ID; the sender must be the person; an ambiguous reply matches nothing and is listed

modules.name: stories
modules.responsibility: Stories turns a topic's judged claims into ranked candidate videos, each with its evidence audit, and merges the reviewer's semantic pass.

d: claims that answer it, audit, readiness
objects.writer: npm run stories -- discover
objects.valid: derived, never hand-edited; references only, no passage text; the evidence gate decides readiness and fails closed

objects.writer: the stories.md agent, or a person
objects.valid: keyed by stable ids; names a current candidate; applicability may narrow, never widen; a chain never nests

modules.name: storyboard
modules.responsibility: Storyboard fills the planner's scenes with the script's own narration, times them, and checks every chart figure and on-screen citation against the evidence package.

objects.writer: the storyboard.md agent; npm run script -- storyboard fills and checks it
objects.valid: no narration of its own; chart data is numeric points with a unit and a cite; assets registered by id

modules.name: topic-discovery
modules.responsibility: Topic proposals per institution (Milestone 2, phase 4; spec §5.1): an agent proposes, an independent agent reviews, code validates and ranks, weak proposals are parked with the reason, and only a person approves or rejects. Nothing here researches: no fetch, no store write, no file under topics/. The module never becomes a second evidence implementation (src/modules/README.md, boundary 1).
modules.paths: src/modules/topic-discovery/ (proposals.ts: validation, ranking, inspection of proposals/<slug>.json and its review)

d: proposed until a person approves or rejects
objects.writer: the discovery agent (discover.md): new files only
objects.valid: validateProposal: a question no story or earlier proposal asks; status moves only by topics approve|reject (a person) or park (code)

d: judges fit and feasibility; parks the weak
objects.writer: the review agent (proposal-review.md), never the proposer
objects.valid: validateReview: one review per proposal; the batch parks on fit false or under topics.minOverall

d: pb-<id> in each listed proposal: one mail
a week; APPROVE <slug> or REJECT by reply
objects.writer: npm run topics -- batch (code); sent records the Message-ID
objects.valid: a pb- id signed with APPROVAL_SECRET, listed per institution; a reply applies once per batch and slug

modules.name: video
modules.responsibility: Video owns the media of a story: narration, the timeline, the Remotion render (scene chunks, the end card), the soundtrack mix, QA and the render check of its bespoke graphics. Packaging owns the review package made from it; publishing owns the ledger.
modules.paths: src/modules/video/ (remotion/, bespoke/, tts/, render-check.ts, final.ts), music/

objects.writer: npm run video -- init from the storyboard; a graphics agent registers bespoke kinds
objects.valid: every scene names a kind the registry accepts; a cue names a spoken word; an unsupported scene fails the build

d: segment.mp4 named by its sha; build-report;
objects.writer: npm run video -- spike (draft, edge voice) and final (release, Azure voice); package writes review/
objects.valid: QA RESULT: PASSED; the package refuses an mp4 whose sha QA did not check; a clearance is recorded, never implied

objects.writer: npm run music -- cues; import keeps licence.cleared, intensity and loop
objects.valid: cues over scene anchors, never seconds; the mix keeps the peak under the ceiling by turning the music down, never the narration

modules.name: website
modules.responsibility: Website owns rendering, the content graph and building and deploying the site. It renders article-release.json and never decides whether a finding needs a correction (article owns corrections and reaffirmations). The Astro folders (src/pages, components, layouts, styles, admin, tools) and astro.config.mjs are part of it and stay where Astro needs them; they import site-graph.ts directly.
modules.paths: src/modules/website/ (graph, SEO, CTA, review page model and job, rehearsal), src/pages, src/components, src/layouts, src/styles, src/admin, src/tools, astro.config.mjs

d: cta.json from cta.md: destinations in the
content graph; a paid one needs your name
objects.writer: an agent (cta.md); links -- cta approve records a person’s approval of a paid link
objects.valid: a destination whose value check fails is dropped; a commercial one needs a disclosure and a person’s approvedBy and is never primary
